how_to_read.prong: H8 is decomposed into four prongs P1 published / P2 drone mesh / P3 Sionna-class engine / P4 validated scattering amplitude. A paper refutes H8 only by satisfying all four at once.

H8.claim_as_stated: ZERO published papers compute a validated scattering signature from a drone mesh in a Sionna-class engine.
H8.verdict: VERIFIED (survives), but only in its literal four-prong form. The two qualifications below are mandatory at every use, because the natural paraphrases of H8 are FALSE.

what_would_refute_it.statement: A single paper that simultaneously satisfies all four prongs.
what_would_refute_it.P1_published: Appears in a peer-reviewed venue (journal, conference proceedings, standards-body proceedings). An arXiv-only manuscript does not count; an arXiv manuscript whose base version is stated in the manuscript to be accepted at a named peer-reviewed venue does count (see Sagitta).
what_would_refute_it.P2_drone_mesh: The UAV is represented by a 3-D surface mesh of the airframe. A metallic cube, a point scatterer, a single rotor blade, or an abstract complex coefficient does not count.
what_would_refute_it.P3_sionna_class_engine: The scattered field is computed INSIDE a Sionna-class differentiable GPU ray engine (Sionna RT, an in-place extension of it, or an equivalent GPU path-tracing EM engine). An RCS computed in FEKO / CST / FDTD and then multiplied into ray-traced paths does NOT count - that is injection, and it is precisely the alternative route our report catalogues.
what_would_refute_it.P4_validated_amplitude: The computed scattering AMPLITUDE (RCS, reflectivity, or echo power) is compared against measurement or against a reference full-wave / analytic solution. Agreement in Doppler-frequency position, rotation period, or spectrogram ridge shape is kinematic and does NOT satisfy P4, because those quantities are insensitive to scattering-amplitude error.
what_would_refute_it.does_it_exist: No. Across 178 paper PDFs in both archives plus the 21-paper passive-radar corpus, no document satisfies all four. The prong-by-prong adjudication of every candidate is in h8_candidates below.

mandatory_qualification_1.text: H8 must never be paraphrased as 'nobody has computed a drone's bistatic RCS for passive WiFi detection'. That paraphrase is FALSE and we can prove it false from our own corpus.
mandatory_qualification_1.counter_paper: Rzewuski, Kulpa, Pachwicewicz, Malanowski, Salski, 'Drone Detectability Feasibility Study using Passive Radars Operating in WIFI and DVB-T Band', NATO STO-MP-MSG-SET-183, paper 13 (PDF metadata author 'Stanislaw Rzewuski', subject 'MSG-SET-183')
mandatory_qualification_1.pdf: /data/public/jeong/papers/Wifi/21_Drone Detectability Feasibility Study using Passive Radars Operating in WIFI and DVB-T Band.pdf

quotes.text: Mono- and bi-static radar cross-sections (RCS) of the Parrot AR.Drone 2.0 were computed with a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method implemented in the commercial software package, QuickWave-3D [2,3].

It is clearly visible that Parrot drone (bistatic) RCS characteristics is not symmetrical (confirmed by the measurements [3]) and it varies with the illuminating signal frequency. The most important is that the RCS range for WIFI band is between -40dBsm and 0dBsm (and average around -20dBsm). For DVB-T frequencies the RCS characteristics varies from -60dBsm to -20dBsm

mandatory_qualification_1.why_it_matters: This 2021 paper delivers the same end-product we aim at - a drone's bistatic RCS at the WiFi band, fed into a passive-radar coverage budget, closed with an OTA detection experiment (successful detection at 50 m bistatic range, p9). It fails only P3: the engine is FDTD, not a ray engine. Our novelty is therefore about the ENGINE and the pipeline integration, not about the existence of the quantity.

prong_scorecard.P2: yes (Parrot AR.Drone 2.0 geometry in an FDTD grid)
prong_scorecard.P4: partial - the asymmetry is 'confirmed by the measurements [3]' and RCS estimation/measurement detail is deferred to reference [4]; no in-paper amplitude overlay

mandatory_qualification_2.text: The word 'published' is carrying the whole claim. If preprints are admitted, the gap closes to a seam: LAMBDA (preprint) already ships UAV RCS alongside Sionna RT paths in one pipeline, and Ziganshin (preprint journal) already validates mesh scattering inside Sionna against measurement. Neither does both at once and neither is peer-reviewed, but the report must say this out loud rather than let 'zero published' imply 'nobody is close'.

sionna_engine_premise_now_first_hand.note: H8 presumes the stock Sionna engine produces no scattering signature. That premise was graded second-hand (X-C13). Both primary documents are on disk and were read this session.
sionna_engine_premise_now_first_hand.precise_wording_required: Sionna RT DOES use shooting-and-bouncing of rays - p1: 'For CIRs, Sionna RT integrates shooting and bouncing of rays (SBR) with the image method and uses a hashing-based mechanism to efficiently eliminate duplicate paths. Radio maps are computed using a purely SBR-based approach.' What it lacks is a physical-optics surface-current integral and any RCS output. Its rough-surface model is an empirical normalized scattering pattern (p51: 'f_s(k_i, k_s, n) is the scattering pattern, which has similarities with the BSDF in computer graphics') driven by a scalar scattering coefficient S (p50). So write 'no PO surface integral, no RCS output', never 'no SBR'.
sionna_engine_premise_now_first_hand.verdict: VERIFIED first-hand. X-C13 can be closed and both documents re-graded from [W] to [P].

H3.verdict: VERIFIED - every element confirmed against the published PDF, plus one provenance defect found (table_v_provenance_defect).
H3.version_note: The 15-page PDF is the published JSAC version; the 13-page PDF is arXiv:2505.20673. Same work. Terminology differs: the published version says AAV where the arXiv version says UAV. Quote the version you actually read.

verified_items.quote: To address this, we introduce a third component, B2, to account for these fluctuations sigma(f, phi) = A(f) x B1(f, phi) x B2. (13)

items.over_claim_to_avoid: The paper is NOT free of scattering amplitude. Eq.(3) on p3 carries 'r_P is the RCS of the point scatterer P', and the body has an explicit alternative model fed by measured reflectivity - p8: 'The Gaussian body model assumes a smoothly distributed RCS centered on the drone's mass center. This is clearly a simplification, as real drone bodies exhibit intricate reflectivity patterns that depend on the shape, material and aspect angle.' The defensible sentence is 'never prints an absolute RCS in dBsm; all model-vs-measurement comparisons are on normalised signatures'.

bonus_settled.finding: The Proc. IEEE 'Clutter-Aware ISAC' PDF DOES use Sionna, with imported meshes. pw04_data.py's EXCLUDED entry (Sionna, ray tracing and mesh not used at all; target as an abstract complex coefficient) is false for this document.

proof.quote: The ToI and UAVs are modeled as simplified 3-D mesh objects imported into Sionna. These meshes are obtained by simplifying publicly available 3-D models in Blender and exporting them in Sionna's XML format, which keeps the ray-tracing scene lightweight while enabling flexible material assignment.

bonus_settled.finding: Both Sionna RT primary documents were read this session. 'physical optics' = 0, 'radar cross section' / 'RCS' = 0, 'dBsm' = 0 in BOTH. The path solver is SBR plus the image method; rough-surface scattering is an empirical normalised scattering pattern with a scalar coefficient S.

quotes.quote: For CIRs, Sionna RT integrates shooting and bouncing of rays (SBR) with the image method and uses a hashing-based mechanism to efficiently eliminate duplicate paths. Radio maps are computed using a purely SBR-based approach.
f_s(k_i, k_s, n) is the scattering pattern, which has similarities with the BSDF in computer graphics [7, Ch. 4.3.1]. The scattering pattern must be normalized to satisfy the condition
we denote by S^2 the fraction of the reflected energy that is diffusely scattered, where S in [0, 1] is the so-called scattering coefficient [41]
